title: Diff as a tour: how a branch's changes become a reading
description: This branch adds one computation — for every function the branch changed, which entrypoints reach it and by what path — and reads it two ways: a generated tour in execution order, and a blast-radius count on a changed frame's header. Read it the way a request does: the endpoint, then down into the diff, the reach, and the tour it renders; then the small wiring in main. The generated "Changes vs origin/main" tour next to this one lists all 31 functions with the facts; this is the story.

stops.description: Both features must never disagree about what reaches what, so there is one endpoint and one answer behind it. [[at:if s.differ == nil]] Without a base there is no "changed", and an empty list would read as "nothing changed" — so it refuses, with the flag to pass. The work is in [[server.Server.diffTourCached]], opened below with everything it reaches.

Listing the changed set reads every function of the project on both sides, so the answer is computed once per index and dropped on reload (see [[server.Server.NotifyReload]], near the end). [[at:changes, deleted, err := s.differ.Changed(s.engine)]] Three steps: what changed, what reaches it, how to say it.

The differ already compared one frame with its twin in the base engine; what it couldn't do was enumerate. [[at:lister, ok := head.(model.FunctionLister)]] A new optional engine interface supplies the list, and identity stays the package-qualified target id, which is why the two engines can be rooted in different directories. [[at:if bl, ok := d.base.(model.FunctionLister); ok]] A function the base had and head doesn't is counted, not listed: there is nothing to open.

The indexer's half of that interface: its own functions with a body, in source order, labelled by display title. [[at:if fi.body == nil || !i.ownsCode(fi)]] Ownership is by path, so vendored and stdlib code — loaded for resolution — can never show up as changed.

The LCS that marked added lines now reports the removed side too, for the +N −M in a stop's description. [[at:if n*m > lineDiffCap]] The cap moved from 3000 cells — about 55 lines a side, so most handlers reported no counts at all — to a million.

The heart of it. [[at:onPath := map[model.TargetID]bool{}]] Backwards first: from every change, walk callers until entrypoints are met, recording the shortest path from each. [[at:sort.SliceStable(order]] The entrypoint reaching the most changes tells its story first. [[at:walk = func(id model.TargetID)]] Then forwards from each entrypoint, callees in call order, staying on the paths found — a change is listed where it is first met, and the ones nothing reaches close the list.

Where execution starts, named for a reader. [[at:case fi.pkg != nil && fi.pkg.Name == "main"]] Narrower on purpose than the reachability seeds, which count every function of a main package so that no RPC is missed: here main is the way in, and its helpers are reached through it rather than being ways in of their own.

A plain BFS over callers with parent pointers; entrypoints are collected in the order met, so the nearest is first and its path is the shortest. [[difftour.graph.callers]] is opened below: [[at:u.Kind == model.UsageRef]] a value reference is not followed, because a function passed as a callback has no call site and a chain through one isn't an execution path — the same line the callers tree draws.

Forwards reads Frame.Calls in source order, so the tour visits callees the way the code does. [[at:for _, cand := range c.Candidates]] Interface candidates and fan-out receivers all count, mirroring the reverse index routesTo walks. If the two ever disagreed a change could be found backwards and never emitted forwards; [[difftour.Compute]] keeps a fallback for exactly that.

A stop should show the change in the context it runs in, so each stop pre-expands the other changed functions whose nearest path passes through it, written as the path from here on — the same `a > b` an author writes. [[at:path := f.Routes[0].Path]] Nearest paths only; expanding every route would open one function several times.

The facts rendered as a tour. [[at:Name:      "diff:" + base]] The name can't be a file — ":" and "/" aren't allowed in one — so it never shadows a tour someone wrote. [[difftour.describe]], opened below, writes each stop from what is known: the kind and size of the change, the nearest entrypoint and the hops, what opens below.

[[line:+61]] The merge-base commit is kept alongside the differ, [[line:+76]] so the tour can say what "changes" are relative to, [[line:+94]] and handed to the server next to the differ it already had. Nothing else in the launch path changed.
[[line:+0-5]] The diff tour was computed against the previous index, so a rebuild drops the cache before telling the page to reload; the next request recomputes and the page refetches.
[[line:+17]] Annotate keeps doing what it did — the per-line highlight — now reading the head side of [[diff.lineDiff]]; [[line:+20]] nothing a frame showed before changed.

[[line:+1]] Kept as a one-line wrapper so the tests that pin the highlight behaviour still read the same. It is the last stop because nothing reaches it from an entrypoint — only tests call it — which the generated tour says outright.
